name: Federal regulation

subjectOf.text: The largest group of respondents, 26.5 percent, estimated annual compliance cost for all federal regulations at between $100,000 and $200,000, while a smaller group of 14.3 percent estimated it at more than $400,000 a year.
subjectOf.abstract: The largest number of respondents (26.5%), however, estimated the annual compliance cost for all federal regulations at between $100,000 and $200,000. A smaller group (14.3%) estimated the cost of compliance as more than $400,000 a year.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: all federal regulations pertaining to private fund advisers, not only Dodd-Frank

subjectOf.text: For all federal regulations, 65.1 percent of respondents estimate total compliance time at between 100 and 500 hours, while a noticeable minority of 20.9 percent estimate it above 1000 hours.
subjectOf.abstract: 65.1% of respondents estimate the total time required to comply with all federal regulations at between 100 and 500 hours. However, a noticeable minority (20.9%) estimate it above 1000 hours.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: all federal rules and procedures including Treasury, SEC, and CFTC
